messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool dp-tidepoint-01 GPU utilization 98% — queue depth increasing. Pager: @Ryan (oncall).
Ryan (oncall): I'm on it. seeing OOM queueing on tenant tidepoint, single-tenant dedicated pool.
Ana SRE: Confirmed. telemetry shows steady GPU sat for 12m, 95-99% usage. latency spikes to 2.5s p95 for generation.
Mike (runtime): Logs: `dp-tidepoint-01` kernel stalls, KV cache churn high. possible heavy long-context jobs.
Lina (support): Customer (TidePoint) reporting timeouts during nightly inference batch. Their PM says ~30% errors since 23:10 UTC.
Jess (AM): looping in customer contact: @tidepoint-admin — we may need to evict or burst. Any constraints on preempting jobs?
tidepoint-admin: They're in the middle of a large rerank and can't restart all jobs. Prefer we avoid evicting active jobs if possible.
Ryan (oncall): Options: 1) Trigger autoscale burst (uses shared burst quota, additional GPUs) 2) Evict lower-priority jobs in pool 3) Route some traffic to compatible smaller model variant. Thoughts?
Ana SRE: Burst quota available but limited (2 nodes). If we burst we can relieve load for ~20-30m. Eviction would free more but needs customer consent.
Mike (runtime): Quick check commands: 
```
# pool status
redwoodctl pools describe dp-tidepoint-01 --region=us-west-2
redwoodctl metrics gpu-util --pool dp-tidepoint-01 --last=15m
```
Outputs show 8/8 GPUs saturated, queued=420, avg latency rising.
Ryan (oncall): I'll propose immediate short burst + throttle incoming non-prod routes. Can we auto-fallback to conv-opt-7b for small requests?
Mike (runtime): We can enable model variant routing for non-critical API keys. Need ~2-3 minutes to flip routing rule.
Lina (support): I'll draft a short message to TidePoint explaining mitigation steps and ETA.
Jess (AM): TidePoint — we request permission to either 1) use burst capacity for 30m to clear backlog, or 2) evict queued non-critical jobs (we'll coordinate which). Which do you prefer?
tidepoint-admin: Please use burst first. We want eviction only if burst doesn't stabilize. Keep us informed.
Ana SRE: Initiating burst now. `redwoodctl pools burst --pool dp-tidepoint-01 --nodes=2`
incident-bot: ACTION: burst requested by Ryan (oncall) at 1801234580. Status: provisioning.
Mike (runtime): Provisioning looks good. GPUs coming up, expected capacity +25%. Watch queue.
Ana SRE: After burst, queue dropped from 420 -> 160 in 4m, p95 latency back to 1.1s.
Ryan (oncall): Good. Keep monitoring 15m. If utilization stays >92% after burst cooldown, we'll plan eviction and notify TidePoint again.
Lina (support): TidePoint notified (sent message at 23:18 UTC). They acknowledged.
Jess (AM): I'll open a follow-up with TidePoint to discuss long-term options: reserved extra capacity or scheduled rerank windows.
Mike (runtime): Post-incident action: evaluate KV cache sizing for their large-context reranks and suggest quantization profile to reduce memory.
Ana SRE: Marking incident as mitigation-in-progress. Will update when we decide to scale further or evict.
Ryan (oncall): Handoff to next oncall in ~25m. @Ana SRE will continue primary watch; I'll update OPS channel and close handoff when stable. :thumbsup:
